what: Estimate yield for one species and area
title: Prediction examples
text: Choose forest measure, species, stand age, type area, area name tile ID. following examples estimate AGB volume black spruce tile H14 three stand ages: function works individual species broad groups coniferous broadleaf:
code: predict_rsyc("agb", "PICE.MAR", c(20, 60, 120), "tile", "H14") #> [1] 27.49419 60.21335 74.19827 predict_rsyc("volume", "PICE.MAR", c(20, 60, 120), "tile", "H14") #> [1]  40.10655 100.42185 127.42231 species_predictions <- tibble::tibble(   species = c("PICE.MAR", "PINU.BAN", "POPU.TRE", "coniferous", "broadleaf") ) |>   dplyr::mutate(     agb_80 = purrr::map_dbl(       species,       \(species) predict_rsyc("agb", species, 80, "tile", "H14")     )   )  species_predictions #> # A tibble: 5 × 2 #>   species    agb_80 #>   <chr>       <dbl> #> 1 PICE.MAR     67.3 #> 2 PINU.BAN     40.6 #> 3 POPU.TRE     80.3 #> 4 coniferous   54.3 #> 5 broadleaf    79.6

title: Prediction examples
text: following example estimates yield several combinations forest measure, species, stand age, tile. row tile_inputs describes one combination: estimating many combinations, use species_in_tile() available_rsyc_models() confirm published curve available species tile.
code: tile_inputs <- tidyr::crossing(   response = c("agb", "volume"),   species = c("PICE.MAR", "POPU.TRE", "coniferous"),   age = c(20, 60, 120),   strata_level = "tile",   strata_id = c("H14", "F31") ) |>   dplyr::mutate(     prediction = purrr::pmap_dbl(       list(response, species, age, strata_level, strata_id),       predict_rsyc     )   )  tile_inputs #> # A tibble: 36 × 6 #>    response species      age strata_level strata_id prediction #>    <chr>    <chr>      <dbl> <chr>        <chr>          <dbl> #>  1 agb      coniferous    20 tile         F31             41.8 #>  2 agb      coniferous    20 tile         H14             27.3 #>  3 agb      coniferous    60 tile         F31             76.6 #>  4 agb      coniferous    60 tile         H14             50.1 #>  5 agb      coniferous   120 tile         F31             87.8 #>  6 agb      coniferous   120 tile         H14             57.4 #>  7 agb      PICE.MAR      20 tile         F31             34.3 #>  8 agb      PICE.MAR      20 tile         H14             27.5 #>  9 agb      PICE.MAR      60 tile         F31             75.2 #> 10 agb      PICE.MAR      60 tile         H14             60.2 #> # ℹ 26 more rows

text: Use area name occurs selected ecological level: Use rsyc_strata() list area names see lie within Canada’s ecological classification. example, one ecodistrict named Muskwa curve species forest measure:
code: eco_inputs <- tibble::tribble(   ~response, ~species,   ~age, ~strata_level, ~strata_id,   "agb",     "PICE.MAR", 80,  "ecozone",     "Atlantic Maritime",   "agb",     "PICE.MAR", 80,  "ecoprovince",     "Appalachian-Acadian Highlands",   "agb",     "PICE.MAR", 80,  "ecoregion",     "Appalachians",   "agb",     "PICE.MAR", 80,  "ecodistrict",     "Windsor Lowlands" )  eco_inputs <- eco_inputs |>   dplyr::mutate(     prediction = purrr::pmap_dbl(       list(response, species, age, strata_level, strata_id),       predict_rsyc     )   )  eco_inputs[c("strata_level", "strata_id", "prediction")] #> # A tibble: 4 × 3 #>   strata_level strata_id                     prediction #>   <chr>        <chr>                              <dbl> #> 1 ecozone      Atlantic Maritime                   71.7 #> 2 ecoprovince  Appalachian-Acadian Highlands       86.2 #> 3 ecoregion    Appalachians                        85.1 #> 4 ecodistrict  Windsor Lowlands                    50.2 rsyc_strata("agb", "PICE.MAR", "ecodistrict") |>   dplyr::filter(strata_name == "Muskwa") #> # A tibble: 2 × 3 #>   strata_level strata_name strata_id                                             #>   <chr>        <chr>       <chr>                                                 #> 1 ecodistrict  Muskwa      Boreal Cordillera/Hay-Slave Lowlands/Muskwa Plateau/… #> 2 ecodistrict  Muskwa      Taiga Plains/Hay-Slave Lowlands/Muskwa Plateau/Muskwa  predict_rsyc(   "agb", "PICE.MAR", 80, "ecodistrict",   "Boreal Cordillera/Hay-Slave Lowlands/Muskwa Plateau/Muskwa" ) #> [1] 75.99985

text: example estimates yield ages 1 150 species area listed curve_inputs: final table, curve_predictions, can plotted used analysis. AGB volume shown separate panels use different units:

")   ) |>   ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(age, prediction, colour = curve)) +   ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +   ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(response), scales = "free_y") +   ggplot2::labs(     x = "Stand age (years)",     y = "Predicted yield",     colour = "Species and tile"   ) +   ggplot2::theme_minimal() +   ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")

what: Remote Sensing-Derived Yield Curves for Canada
title: Remote Sensing-Derived Yield Curves for Canada
text: RSYC provides published yield curves aboveground biomass (AGB, Mg/ha) total volume (m3/ha). Curves available individual species generic, coniferous, broadleaf model groups. Models available 150 x 150 km tiles four nested ecological levels: ecozone, ecoprovince, ecoregion, ecodistrict. Species-specific RSYC curves across Canada’s 150 km tile grid.

title: Remote Sensing-Derived Yield Curves for Canada
text: don’t need install R package use models. model parameters used RSYC available direct download. ZIP archive contains updated RSYC_models.csv table, including AGB volume models tiles ecological strata. Model parameters: RSYC_models.zip Tile grid: RSYC_tiles.gpkg Ecological strata: RSYC_ecostrat.gpkg RSYC models predict aboveground biomass (AGB) total volume function stand age: \[ y = b_1 e^{-b_4 \mathrm{Age}} (1 - e^{-b_2 \mathrm{Age}})^{b_3}. \] \(y\) AGB (Mg/ha) total volume (m3/ha) \(b_1, b_2, b_3, b_4\) response-, stratum-, species-specific parameters Age stand age (years) curves fitted stand ages 1 150 years. RSYC warns asked estimate outside age range. Age 0 also allowed starting point curve.

title: Remote Sensing-Derived Yield Curves for Canada
text: following example produces complete set estimates ages 1 150 species area listed curve_inputs: Plot curves compare predicted yield changes stand age. AGB volume shown separately use different units:  See Prediction examples longer walkthrough, including model-availability checks.
code: curve_inputs <- tibble::tribble(   ~response, ~species,    ~strata_level, ~strata_id,   "agb",     "PICE.MAR",  "tile",       "H14",   "agb",     "POPU.TRE",  "tile",       "F31",   "volume",  "coniferous", "tile",       "N3" ) curve_inputs <- curve_inputs |>   dplyr::mutate(     age = list(1:150),     prediction = purrr::pmap(       list(response, species, age, strata_level, strata_id),       predict_rsyc     )   )  curve_inputs #> # A tibble: 3 × 6 #>   response species    strata_level strata_id age         prediction  #>   <chr>    <chr>      <chr>        <chr>     <list>      <list>      #> 1 agb      PICE.MAR   tile         H14       <int [150]> <dbl [150]> #> 2 agb      POPU.TRE   tile         F31       <int [150]> <dbl [150]> #> 3 volume   coniferous tile         N3        <int [150]> <dbl [150]>  curve_predictions <- curve_inputs |>   tidyr::unnest(c(age, prediction)) curve_predictions |>   dplyr::mutate(     response = factor(       response,       levels = c("agb", "volume"),       labels = c("AGB (Mg/ha)", "Volume (m3/ha)")     ),     curve = paste(species, strata_id, sep = " - ")   ) |>   ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(age, prediction, colour = curve)) +   ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +   ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(response), scales = "free_y") +   ggplot2::labs(     x = "Stand age (years)",     y = "Predicted yield",     colour = "Species and tile"   ) +   ggplot2::theme_minimal() +   ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: Remote Sensing-Derived Yield Curves for Canada
text: Three functions provided help identify model use: available_rsyc_models() lists individual published curves match response, species, type area, area name. example, list volume curves black spruce ecozone level: rsyc_species() lists species available selected response area. also gives species’ common name model group. example, list AGB species available tile H14: rsyc_strata() lists areas models available selected response species. gives short area name full hierarchical area identifier, can distinguish repeated area names. example, list ecozones volume models black spruce:
code: available_rsyc_models(   response = "volume",   species = "PICE.MAR",   strata_level = "ecozone" ) rsyc_species(response = "agb", strata_level = "tile", strata_id = "H14") rsyc_strata(   response = "volume",   species = "PICE.MAR",   strata_level = "ecozone" )

what: Generate multiple yield curves for species and areas
title: Remote Sensing-Derived Yield Curves for Canada
text: rsyc_product() prepares yield estimates matching area boundaries. boundaries stored separately map shape repeated every species stand age. default, function estimates ages 1 150: spatial map contains strata_id, ecological area names, area shapes. tiles, contains strata_id tile shapes. curves table records model, area, species, stand age, estimated yield. metadata table summarizes units, model version, equation, choices used create results. Use output = "rsyc_volume.gpkg" save map, yield curves, summary information together one GeoPackage file.
code: product <- rsyc_product(   response = "volume",   species = c("PICE.MAR", "POPU.TRE"),   age = 1:200,   strata_level = "ecodistrict" )  product$spatial product$curves product$metadata
